metadata.title: Everolimus Monotherapy
metadata.indication: 00320a: advanced RCC after VEGF-targeted therapy; 00320b: progressive unresectable/metastatic well/moderately differentiated pancreatic NET; 00320c: progressive unresectable/metastatic well-differentiated G1/G2 non-functional GI NET.
metadata.partial_assessment_note: Any independently actionable entered value is assessed; omitted domains remain unassessed and do not block a partial result.

provenance.source: NCCP 00320 v6 / NET and GU catalogues

metadata.partial_assessment_policy: Each entered value is assessed independently. Organ-function values or categories are optional; omitted domains remain unassessed and are never assumed normal.

catalogue_reconciliation.scope_note: The NCCP states that its website list is not comprehensive. This reconciliation does not assert that every possible national regimen is published online.

encoding_maturity.label: Source-reconciled full everolimus pathway · independent clinical/pharmacy review pending

organ_function_reconciliation.note: NCCP Table2 hepatic doses preserved as standard-dose targets with baseline/prior-dose/ChildC benefit-risk guards. EMA explicitly leaves adverse-event dose modification in hepatic impairment without supporting clinical data; specialist review prevents unsafe automatic table combination.

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: The treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist or other appropriately authorised specialist named in the current NCCP source.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Use the most restrictive applicable component rule and confirm dose changes against the current official NCCP PDF.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Decision-support encoding includes NCCP 00320 Version 6. It does not replace the current official regimen, prescribing review, pharmacy verification or independent clinical judgement.
clinical_governance.organ_function_rule_status: Source reconciled in SACTCheck v0.59.0; independent Consultant and oncology-pharmacy validation pending.

indications.description: Advanced renal-cell carcinoma that has progressed on or after VEGF-targeted therapy.
Unresectable or metastatic, well- or moderately-differentiated pancreatic neuroendocrine tumour in an adult with progressive disease.
Unresectable or metastatic, well-differentiated Grade 1 or 2 non-functional gastrointestinal neuroendocrine tumour in an adult with progressive disease.

treatment.schedule_summary: Everolimus 10 mg orally once daily continuously. A 28-day interval is an administrative review period, not a tablet-free cycle.
treatment.duration_text: Continue while clinical benefit persists and toxicity remains acceptable, according to the consultant treatment plan.
treatment.schedule_interval_label: Continuous daily treatment; review every 4 weeks

components.note: Same time every day, consistently with or without food. Swallow whole with a glass of water; do not chew/crush. Missed dose: no additional dose; take next prescribed dose as usual.

hypersensitivity.label: Hypersensitivity to everolimus, another rapamycin derivative or an excipient

alt_ast_uln_multiple.label: ALT / AST result (actual values entered; highest ×ULN calculated automatically)
alt_ast_uln_multiple.assessment_guidance: Retained clinical context. NCCP 00320 v6 does not specify an isolated ALT/AST or bilirubin ×ULN dose cutoff. Assess Child–Pugh class, treatment-related toxicity and the complete clinical picture; no unsupported numeric LFT hold is calculated.

bilirubin_uln_multiple.label: Bilirubin result (actual value entered; ×ULN calculated automatically)
bilirubin_uln_multiple.assessment_guidance: Retained clinical context. NCCP 00320 v6 does not specify an isolated ALT/AST or bilirubin ×ULN dose cutoff. Assess Child–Pugh class, treatment-related toxicity and the complete clinical picture; no unsupported numeric LFT hold is calculated.

oral_toxicity_grade.label: Current other non-haematological toxicity grade (excluding stomatitis, pneumonitis and metabolic events)

options.label: Grade 1 — Mild
options.description: Grade 1 under the named CTCAE term: generally mild or asymptomatic, with observation only and no intervention indicated.

options.label: Grade 2 — Moderate
options.description: Grade 2 under the named CTCAE term: generally moderate; local/non-invasive intervention may be indicated and instrumental activities may be limited.

options.label: Grade 3 — Severe
options.description: Grade 3 under the named CTCAE term: severe or medically significant; hospital care may be indicated and self-care activities may be limited.

options.label: Grade 4 — Life-threatening
options.description: Grade 4 under the named CTCAE term: life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

oral_toxicity_grade.assessment_guidance: Identify and grade the specific toxicity using its CTCAE definition; assess symptoms, intervention and functional impact. NCCP 00320 v6 Table 3 supplies the action, but does not state the CTCAE edition. The related EMA Table 1 uses CTCAE v3.0. The existing CTCAE v5 descriptors shown here are supplementary orientation only; confirm the source-grade interpretation clinically and do not assume the editions are interchangeable.

stomatitis_grade.label: Stomatitis grade

options.label: Grade 1 — Mild
options.description: Asymptomatic or mild symptoms; intervention not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2 — Moderate
options.description: Moderate pain or ulceration that does not interfere with oral intake; modified diet indicated.

options.label: Grade 3 — Severe
options.description: Severe pain that interferes with oral intake.

stomatitis_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess pain, ulceration and ability to maintain oral intake. NCCP 00320 v6 Table 3 supplies the action, but does not state the CTCAE edition. The related EMA Table 1 uses CTCAE v3.0. The existing CTCAE v5 descriptors shown here are supplementary orientation only; confirm the source-grade interpretation clinically and do not assume the editions are interchangeable.

noninfectious_pneumonitis_grade.label: Non-infectious pneumonitis grade

options.label: Grade 1 — Mild
options.description: Asymptomatic; clinical or diagnostic observations only; intervention not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2 — Moderate
options.description: Symptomatic; medical intervention indicated; limits instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3 — Severe
options.description: Severe symptoms; oxygen indicated; limits self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4 — Life-threatening
options.description: Life-threatening respiratory compromise; urgent intervention such as ventilatory support required.

noninfectious_pneumonitis_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess symptoms, oxygen requirement, imaging and functional impact. NCCP 00320 v6 Table 3 supplies the action, but does not state the CTCAE edition. The related EMA Table 1 uses CTCAE v3.0. The existing CTCAE v5 descriptors shown here are supplementary orientation only; confirm the source-grade interpretation clinically and do not assume the editions are interchangeable.

assessment_type.label: Assessment timing
assessment_type.assessment_guidance: Table 1 concerns treatment toxicity, not an invented baseline blood-count eligibility threshold. A 28-day interval is a review period; tablets are taken continuously.

everolimus_previous_dose_mg.label: Documented daily everolimus dose before this interruption/change
everolimus_previous_dose_mg.assessment_guidance: Do not substitute the standard 10 mg for a missing prescribed dose. Numeric toxicity restart requires an explicitly documented dose and no hepatic impairment; combined hepatic/toxicity adjustments need specialist review.

hepatic_c_benefit_risk_approved.label: Child–Pugh C: specialist benefit–risk decision supports treatment

renal_impairment.label: Renal impairment present
renal_impairment.assessment_guidance: NCCP Table 2: no routine renal dose adjustment; this does not clear acute kidney injury or other toxicity.

acute_kidney_injury.label: Acute kidney injury or clinically important worsening renal function

lowest_anc_episode.label: Lowest neutrophil count in this same interrupted episode

lowest_platelets_episode.label: Lowest platelet count in this same interrupted episode

febrile_neutropenia_episode_grade.label: Highest febrile neutropenia grade in this episode
febrile_neutropenia_episode_grade.assessment_guidance: Grade 3 requires ANC recovery ≥1.25×10⁹/L AND no fever. Grade 4 requires discontinuation. Source grades are not calculated from a single temperature or count.

hbv_screen_positive.label: HBsAg or HBcoreAb positive
hbv_screen_positive.assessment_guidance: Requires the local HBV/hepatology and antiviral management plan; positivity is not an automatic exclusion.

interaction_status.label: Everolimus medicine/food interaction review

options.label: Other relevant interaction or review incomplete

interaction_status.assessment_guidance: EMA SmPC 4.5: avoid interacting combinations where possible. Inhibitor/inducer adjustments and washout are specialist decisions; do not combine automatically with hepatic/toxicity dose tables.

perioperative_or_radiotherapy_concern.label: Peri-operative wound-healing, recent/concurrent radiotherapy or radiation-recall concern

eligibility: Adults with an indication matching NCCP 00320a (post-VEGF advanced RCC), 00320b (progressive pancreatic NET), or 00320c (progressive non-functional G1/G2 GI NET). See the preserved indication records for exact differentiation and stage.
ECOG performance status 0–2; significant pre-existing lung compromise requires caution.
exclusions: Hypersensitivity to everolimus, another rapamycin derivative or excipients.
monitoring: Baseline: FBC, renal and liver profile; BUN and urinary protein; total cholesterol and triglycerides; fasting serum glucose; HBsAg and HBcoreAb (NCCP p2).

During treatment: FBC, renal and liver profile every 4 weeks. Check cholesterol/triglycerides regularly and fasting glucose as clinically indicated; no universal lipid/glucose interval is specified (NCCP p2).
Disease assessment, imaging and tumour markers follow the individual consultant plan; no fixed scan or chromogranin-A interval is mandated by NCCP 00320.

Monitor infection, new respiratory symptoms, oral ulcers, metabolic abnormalities, renal deterioration and interactions. Consider PJP prophylaxis if corticosteroids/immunosuppressants are required; no universal prophylaxis prescription is implied.
dose_modifications: NCCP 00320 v6 Tables 1–3 are encoded by toxicity, recovery, recurrence and documented previous dose; all modifications require consultant discussion.
No independent ALT/AST >5×ULN or bilirubin >3×ULN interruption threshold is present in this regimen source. Use Child–Pugh class and a clinically graded treatment-related toxicity assessment.
NCCP rounded ANC/platelet bands are clarified using EMA Table 1 (<1/<75) without leaving decimal gaps. Baseline low counts are reviewed separately from on-treatment toxicity.

Numeric toxicity restart is suppressed with missing or lower previous dose, hepatic impairment, unresolved recovery, source-discretionary restart or contradictory history. Same-dose restarts require the documented actual dose; never reset automatically to standard 10 mg.

EMA Table 1 uses CTCAE v3.0; NCCP does not specify an edition. Existing CTCAE v5 orientation descriptors are labelled supplementary. Metabolic recovery targets, third/later recurrences and simultaneous hepatic/toxicity adjustments remain individual decisions.

supportive_care.mapping_basis: Risk assigned from the most emetogenic active component and treatment phase.
supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for oral SACT
regimen_specific_notes: Minimal-to-low emetic risk; follow local antiemetic policy.
Alcohol-free prophylactic/therapeutic mouthwash may be required per local policy. Do not present dexamethasone mouthwash as mandatory for every NET patient.
Promptly report new/worsening respiratory symptoms, fever/infection and mouth ulcers. Steroid/PJP prophylaxis and HBV antiviral plans require clinical assessment.
